To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we showed that treatment interruption is safe in patients with a CD4+ cell nadir above 350 cells/mm3, but that no improvement in quality-of-life scores was observed.

stopping treatment in patients with high CD4 T cell nadir was feasible and safe, but no benefit in quality of life or CD4 T cell count could be established, and patients may experience symptoms of ARVS, which may lead to reinitiation of treatment.

we found no improvement in quality-of-life scores after stopping HAART, that we found that patients can experience ARVS (13% of patients), that we found that the risk for the development of resistance after stopping is realistic, and that there is a potential risk for HIV transmission to sexual contacts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the safety of discontinuing HAART in patients who started therapy too early.
the question whether it is safe to interrupt HAART in patients with a CD4+ cell nadir above 350 cells/mm3, who started HAART at a time when this was not recommended by the Dutch national guidelines.
the question whether it is safe to discontinue antiretrovirus therapy in patients who have a high CD4 cell count at the time of starting antiretrovirs therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stopping treatment in patients with a CD4 T-cell count >500 cells/mm3 and CD4 nadir >350 cells/mm is feasible and safe, but the benefits are questionable and the risks are real.
treatment should be continued in patients with a CD4+ cell count of 500-550 cells/mm3 or higher.
treatment interruption in patients with high CD4 T cell counts should be considered with caution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that treatment can be stopped in early starters, but that this is associated with risks and that there is no benefit in doing so.
stopping treatment in patients with a CD4+ cell count >350 cells/ mm3 and no previous treatment is not a safe option.
we have to be careful when we start treatment in early stage HIV patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that treatment can be safely discontinued in patients with a CD4+ nadir of >350 cells/mm³ and that this strategy is feasible in a real-life setting.
patients who have a CD4 T-cell count >500 cells/mm3 should not be started on HAART.

we should be very careful with stopping HAART too early, and we should not do it in patients with a CD4 nadir >350 cells/mm³, because they are at risk for developing resistance and for transmitting the virus to sexual partners.
